# Mini investigation: does compound Z improve flow?

> Score-free research header v1 — test fixture. Assessment: ACH_Eval_NLM_Super, gauge **G = 64**, 1 enabled axis.

## 1. Mission

You are the Investigator. Build the strongest source-grounded case and preserve adverse findings.

## 2. Frozen hypotheses

### **axis one:**
Does compound Z improve urinary flow in adult men with obstruction?

**Governing boundary.** H1 requires measured flow improvement; H2 requires affirmative evidence of no improvement; H3 applies when the evidence cannot decide.

**Cohort:** Adult men with bladder outlet obstruction.

> **Human-review gate:** The analyst reviewed and approved this H1/H2/H3 set on 2026-10-01.

| Hypothesis | Human-written statement |
|---|---|
| **A1-H1** | Compound Z improves maximum urinary flow rate in adult men with bladder outlet obstruction at standard oral doses. |
| **A1-H2** | Compound Z does not improve maximum urinary flow rate in adult men with bladder outlet obstruction at standard oral doses. |
| **A1-H3** | The available evidence cannot determine whether compound Z improves maximum urinary flow rate in these men. |

#### A1-H1 — Z improves flow

**Assumptions and antecedents:** Standard oral doses of compound Z reach the bladder and prostate tissue in adult men.

**Potential falsification:** A randomized trial shows no change in maximum flow rate with compound Z at standard doses.

**Potential corroboration:** Randomized trials report increased maximum flow rate with compound Z compared with placebo.

#### A1-H2 — Z does not improve flow

**Assumptions and antecedents:** Trials of compound Z measured maximum flow rate with adequate sample sizes.

**Potential falsification:** A randomized trial shows a significant increase in maximum flow rate with compound Z.

**Potential corroboration:** Several trials report no significant change in flow with compound Z compared with placebo.

#### A1-H3 — cannot determine

**Assumptions and antecedents:** Meaningful retrieval of the trials of compound Z has been completed.

**Potential falsification:** Consistent trials establish whether compound Z changes maximum flow rate.

**Potential corroboration:** The trials of compound Z are small, conflicting, or measure different endpoints.

## 3. Decisive-test map

| Test | Question the corpus must help answer |
|---|---|
| **Flow** | Does compound Z change maximum flow rate in randomized trials? |
| **Exposure** | Do standard oral doses reach prostate tissue? |
